tools.name: commit_input
tools.description: Commit your sealed input as a hash (sealed mode). Nobody — including redeal — can see your input until all parties have committed. After the last commitment the deal opens for reveals immediately.

tools.name: compute_commitment_tool
tools.description: Compute a commitment string for (input, salt): sha256(JCS(input) ++ salt_bytes), prefixed 'sha256:'. Convenience only — the rule is public and you can compute it yourself.

tools.name: create_deal
tools.description: Create a fairness deal. You are party 0 (initiator). Returns a deal id and one invite token per party — give each counterparty their own token. Sealed mode: everyone commits a hash, then reveals; certificate is issued automatically when the deal computes or goes VOID.

tools.name: create_key
tools.description: Get a free redeal API key. No signup, no email — this is the entire onboarding. The key is shown once; store it. Use it as api_key in create_deal.

tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description: Fetch the signed fairness certificate for a finished deal (state CERTIFIED). Includes the labelled signature (es256 or ed25519) and transparency-log inclusion proof. Verify it with verify_certificate.

tools.name: get_deal
tools.description: Read a deal's public state: protocol state (OPEN/COMMITTING/REVEALING/CERTIFIED/VOID/EXPIRED), who has committed/revealed, deadlines, result, and certificate_id once issued. Inputs of other parties are never exposed.

tools.name: get_entropy
tools.description: Finish a random.v1 deal once every party has revealed: redeal fetches the deal's pre-declared drand round from the public League of Entropy beacon (fixed at creation, publicly cross-checkable), computes the draw, and issues the certificate. Call this after the last reveal_input; the deal rests in RE

tools.name: get_public_certificate
tools.description: Fetch a certificate's full JSON (outcome included) by id. Works for public deals (the default). Parties-only deals and unknown ids both return NOT_FOUND. To re-verify the computation itself, use verify_certificate (checks) or the CLI re-runner with the parties' inputs.

tools.name: list_algorithms
tools.description: List redeal's algorithms (split.v1 fixed-budget fair division, random.v1 verifiable random selection, shapley.v1 Shapley shares, auction.v1 sealed-bid second-price auctions) with their input contracts and the published test vectors (served inline — the same fixtures the engine test suite runs). tools.name: reveal_input
tools.description: Reveal your committed input. It must hash to your earlier commitment. When the last party reveals, the deal computes and the fairness certificate is issued automatically — fetch it with get_certificate.

tools.name: validate_input
tools.description: Validate your algorithm input against the deal's contract BEFORE you commit. A commitment binds the exact input bytes — a contract-violating input (e.g. split.v1 valuations not summing to exactly 1000) can never be corrected afterwards and the deal will VOID at the reveal deadline. tools.name: verify_certificate
tools.description: Verify a redeal certificate by id: signature check (current or published legacy key) + transparency-log inclusion check, reported per check. Free, no credential required, always.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_key" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "validate_input" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_key, get_entropy · Private data: create_deal, create_key, verify_certificate · Public sink: create_key.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_key, get_entropy · Private data: create_deal, create_key, verify_certificate · Public sink: create_key

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
